Description: Over 230 miles of multi-use trail providing opportunities for transportation, exercise and connection to recreational and cultural spaces for Central Ohio residents and visitors. A regional effort and collaboration across Central Ohio municipalities.
Identity Notes: System-level trail network spanning multiple municipalities and potentially multiple counties. Columbus Recreation and Parks designs, builds and manages trail within City of Columbus. MORPC and Central Ohio Greenways Board provide regional coordination. Member trails documented individually as Tier 6 Trail entities.

Identity Notes: 154+ miles of paved bikepath/shared-use paths; managed as network infrastructure (not individually named trails); bikeways GIS layer (FeatureServer/1) has 300+ segments with no named trail identifiers — infrastructure/pavement management data only; Camp Chase Trail and Heritage Trail pass through Dublin and are already documented at Tier 3 (Metro Parks); this record documents the Dublin-managed network system

Partner Agencies: Columbus Recreation and Parks Department; Delaware County; Pickaway County; Ohio DNR
Description: Regional water trail network comprising 100+ miles of paddling routes along five Central Ohio waterways: Alum Creek, Big Darby Creek, Big Walnut Creek, Olentangy River, and Scioto River. Coordinated by MORPC as part of the Central Ohio outdoor recreation infrastructure initiative. Spans Delaware, Franklin, and Pickaway counties.
Identity Notes: Multi-county network; held across Delaware, Franklin, Pickaway counties. MORPC coordinates overall network; individual water trail segments governed by respective municipalities and agencies. Olentangy River Water Trail (FR-T-0001) is the Franklin County member currently documented. Other member trails (Alum Creek, Big Darby Creek, Big Walnut Creek, Scioto River) not yet processed.
Notes: Length estimate is approximate (100+ miles per MORPC website as of 2026). Full member trail enumeration pending discovery of Delaware and Pickaway county segments.
